title: Recollecting the community
hookLine: the credits roll after the movie, and the third old recollection: the people walking the path
tomorrow: can you be glad of your own good deeds without bragging?

lines: THE CREDITS ROLL ON AND ON.
THE ONE, THE WAY, THE PEOPLE.
cards: The credits at the end of a movie roll on and on: camera crew, caterers, the person who coached the accents. Hardly anyone stays to read them, except the people whose names are up there, and their families.
Yesterday's question asked who practices well, and why call them to mind. The third of the old recollections is the credits roll for the path: the sangha, the community.
After the one who showed the way, and the way itself, come the people walking it.

teach.b: The verse opens: supatipanno bhagavato savakasangho. The Blessed One's community of disciples is practicing well. Then: practicing straight, the true way, properly.
It names them as four pairs of persons, eight kinds of individuals: those walking the stages of the path and those who have arrived.
Buddhaghosa says that whoever keeps recalling them comes to feel he's living in the community's company, and when tempted to do wrong, feels it as if they were standing right there.
It's yesterday's teacher-in-the-room, widened to a whole crowd. A path is hard to keep alone for long; it helps to remember who's on it.
And since today looks back, here's the week that led here. Open space, where nothing sticks. The sign appears, and it's guarded.
The body changes. To cool, not to hate. Thus indeed is he.
And now, practicing well: the verse praises a verb, not a rank.

how: Theravada Buddhists chant the recollection of the sangha, supatipanno bhagavato savakasangho, after those of the Buddha and the dhamma; as a meditation its qualities are called to mind one at a time, as Visuddhimagga 7 describes.

o: joining a temple and paying its membership every year
memorizing the names of well-known monks from history
calling to mind the community that's practicing well

games.q: the third recollection — tap the pairs.
p: those on the path, and arrived

s: the sangha verse praises the community for its rank and robes
it praises how they walk: practicing well, straight, the true way, properly.
Buddhaghosa says recalling the community can feel like living in its company
and when tempted to do wrong, it's as if they were standing right there.
the three recollections are of the Buddha, the teaching and the community
the one who showed the way, the way, and the people walking it.

games.q: you're about to drop a habit you care about, a weekly run, after missing two weeks. by today's lesson, what helps most?
o: calling to mind the people who keep at it, and going back with them.
going alone and twice as hard, to make up for the missed weeks.
waiting quietly until you feel motivated again on your own.
games.why: the third recollection is about company: a path is easier to keep when you remember who's walking it with you.

practice: Bring to mind people who practice well in your life, in any sense: someone patient, someone honest, someone who keeps showing up. Count them on your fingers, one by one, and let each face stay a moment.
If you'd like, end with the verse's first word, supatipanno, practicing well.

wordCard.voice: Recollecting the community: calling to mind the sangha, those practicing well, until it feels like walking in their company.

orig.note: Pali: practicing well. The first word of the recollection of the sangha.

carryVoice: Your line: practicing well. A path is easier to keep when you remember who's on it. Day twenty-one of forty.
